newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia trade data spark little action.
newsitem.headline: Australia trade data spark little action.

text.p: Australia's current account deficit, which once drove currency traders into a frenzy, on Monday hit the economists' target of A$1.33 billion (US$1.05 billion) for August and inspired little trading action.
The latest monthly figure widened from July's seasonally adjusted deficit of A$1.21 billion, but represented a welcome fall from the A$1.55 billion deficit struck in August last year.
Economists had on average forecast an August deficit of A$1.3 billion, with estimates ranging from A$1.2 billion to A$1.5 billion.

"The figure is very much in line with expectations," Westpac Banking Corp economist Nigel Stapledon told Reuters. "But the markets are really focussed on bigger things. The balance of payments has very much gone to the back page."
This was in marked contrast to the situation a year ago when the monthly current account was setting record deficits, making it the major focus of the markets.
The trade balance remained in surplus in August, rising to A$195 million from A$109 million in July and compared with a A$156 million deficit at the same time last year.

"It's good to see our trade in surplus, but the net income deficit remains a drag on the economy and it will be a long time before that is pared back," Colonial State Bank chief economist Hans Kunnen said.
Imports rose to A$6.22 billion in August from A$6.15 billion in July, while exports grew to A$6.41 billion from A$6.25 billion previously.

Although seen by economists as a bullish result for bonds, traders' attention was focussed on the Reserve Bank of Australia's (RBA) board meeting on Tuesday and a run of key U.S. data throughout the week.
"The balance of payments numbers can only be read as being bullish for the fixed interest market," said Citibank Australia senior economist Stephen Koukoulas.
After opening weaker in line with a softer U.S. treasury market, 10-year bond yields ended two points higher at 7.79 percent.

The Australian dollar also failed to react to the data with the spotlight firmly on the RBA meeting. At 4.45 pm (0645 GMT), the local dollar had crept cautiously ahead to US$0.7925/30 from US$0.7923/28 late on Friday.
